item.title: The Central Synthesis: One System, Multiple Layers
item.lead: The dossier brings together economics, technology, psychology, demographics, and law into one model of commercialized intimacy.

blocks.text: At the front end is the human promise: attention, recognition, attraction, and proximity. At the back end, according to the source, are CRM profiles, scripts, chat teams, AI tools, payment streams, and international corporate structures. The central thesis is that the distance between these two layers has increased as the system has become more scalable.

The seven parts of this series show that each layer has its own research question. Operations is about who conducts the conversation. Economics is about who receives the money. AI is about who determines the text and timing. Sociology is about what repeated exposure can do to expectations. Law is about who is visible and accountable. The foundation philosophically connects these components.

Together, these questions do not automatically provide proof for all claims in the source. However, a coherent research program emerges: human intimacy is no longer solely an interpersonal phenomenon but also a technical, organizational, and financial process that can be observed and audited.
The final balance of the dossier is therefore strongest when formulated as a systems question, not as an accusation against every individual or every platform.
